points.t: Small pustules, **each pierced by a hair**: beard, scalp, thighs, buttocks, axillae.
Inflamed follicle opening: usually *S. aureus*; also Pseudomonas, Malassezia, irritant / occlusive.
Stop the trigger, **antiseptic wash**; flucloxacillin only if persistent or extensive.
Progression to boils or cellulitis; recurrence (carriage, diabetes); immunosuppression.

cause.lead: A damaged or blocked follicle that bacteria colonise.
points: **Shaving, waxing, tight clothing, oils**, sweat, friction.
*S. aureus* in the follicle opening; **nasal carriage** drives recurrence.
Topical steroids and immunosuppression raise risk.
Not all folliculitis is staph: **hot tub** (Pseudomonas), **Pityrosporum** (Malassezia), Gram-negative, eosinophilic, pseudofolliculitis barbae.

visuals.caption: Depth matters: folliculitis is a superficial pustule at the follicle opening (left); a boil is a deep abscess around one follicle (centre); a carbuncle joins several follicles with multiple heads (right).
visuals.alt: Three skin sections: folliculitis, furuncle and carbuncle

features.lead: Read the history and the distribution.
points: **Follicular pustules** on a red base, often with a central hair.
Scalp, beard (**sycosis barbae**), trunk, buttocks, thighs, axillae.
Itchy or tender; systemic upset unusual.
**Hot tub**: 1–2 days after a spa, under swimwear.
**Pityrosporum**: itchy uniform papules, upper back and chest, after antibiotics.
Distribution + history point to the type.
Shaving, waxing, hot tub, recent antibiotics, steroid creams?
A pustule if persistent, recurrent, extensive or atypical.

cards.name: Acne vulgaris
cards.clue: Comedones; face, chest, back; mixed lesions.

cards.name: Pustular miliaria
cards.clue: Heat and occlusion; pustules not follicle-centred.

cards.name: Candida
cards.clue: Satellite pustules around a red moist fold.

cards.name: Keratosis pilaris
cards.clue: Rough follicular papules, upper arms, thighs; not pustular.

cards.name: Malassezia / Gram-negative
cards.clue: After antibiotics; needs a different treatment.

manage.lead: Most mild cases settle without antibiotics.

points: Change shaving technique (clean sharp blade, with the grain, or pause).
Loose clothing; avoid oils and occlusion.
Topical antiseptic or antibiotic, short course, per local guidance.
Swab; decolonisation via local pathway; screen for diabetes.

items.t: Progression to **boils, carbuncles or cellulitis**, or fever.
Recurrent despite measures: carriage, **PVL** or MRSA, diabetes, immunosuppression.
Widespread itchy folliculitis in immunosuppression (eosinophilic): refer.

pearls.t: Upper back and chest pustules after antibiotics? **Pityrosporum**: needs an antifungal.
Hot-tub history explains a sudden swimsuit-distribution rash.
Mild bacterial folliculitis: a stewardship opportunity.
Pseudofolliculitis barbae in curly hair: discuss shaving and beard growth sensitively.

quiz.q: What is the usual organism in superficial bacterial folliculitis?
Swimsuit-distribution pustules 1–2 days after a spa?
Itchy uniform papules on the upper back after antibiotics?
quiz.a: Pityrosporum (Malassezia) folliculitis: treat with an antifungal.
Stop or modify the trigger and use an antiseptic wash; often no antibiotic needed.

quiz.q: What to check in recurrent folliculitis?
quiz.a: Swab, nasal carriage, diabetes; consider PVL/MRSA and other types.
